payload.headline: Alphabet jumps 6.3% to 282.1, near fair value; hold, add only at 234.35

summary.thesis: Sales are growing faster and margins are rising, but free cash flow has collapsed under heavy spending, so the stock is only fair against its own history and expensive on cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, with no adding above 279.84; swing: wait, because today's jump pays about the same to the next ceiling as it risks to the support zone.
summary.act_at: Add at 234.35; swing entry only on a hold of 271.77–277.07 or a close above 300.07

payload.happening: Alphabet closed at 282.1, up 6.34% in a day. That is back above the 271.77–277.07 support zone it broke on the previous note, but still below its 20-day average of 287.71 and its 50-day average of 320.95, both falling. The only business news is a reported upgrade: TechCrunch says Google Search's AI Mode can now use Drive and Wallet for more personal answers. There is no earnings date in the data.
payload.business: The business itself looks stronger. Quarterly sales grew 24.65% from a year ago, up from 21.79% two quarters ago. The operating margin (profit from the core business per dollar of sales) rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment) fell to 19.7B from 73.6B a year earlier, a margin of only 4.19%. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 24¢ a year, down from 40¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. Reported profit is also inflated. The net margin of 50.03% is above the operating margin because of one-off gains, so underlying earnings are lower than the headline. Analysts are cutting their numbers: this year's EPS estimate fell 5.2% in 30 days, to 19.56. The balance sheet is not at risk, with net cash of 139.0B and liquidity of 265.1B. Today's news changes sentiment, not the numbers. The AI Mode feature is a product step with no reported revenue figure. The CNBC and FT stories do not affect demand, margins or cash.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model (DCF: future cash flows valued in today's money, with a 10.0% discount rate) gives only 26.0 / 51.55 / 70.45 per share for bear / base / bull. That is because it starts from today's depressed 19.7B of free cash flow. Even with 30% starting growth it reaches only 78.38. Against its own history, the price-to-sales ratio puts fair value at 234.35 / 279.84 / 375.22 (low / middle / high). At 282.1, the stock sits right at the middle of that range, at the 43.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. Against peers it looks expensive: price-to-sales is 7.4 against a peer median of 4.7. On earnings it looks cheap at a trailing P/E (price divided by the last 12 months of earnings per share) of 14.8. But that rises to 18.8 on next year's EPS of 14.97, because analysts expect earnings to fall once the one-off gains drop out. The data's valuation summary still quotes the old price of 265.29, so that line is one day out of date. The whole gap between methods comes down to one question: does cash flow recover toward 73.6B or stay near 19.7B? I keep the fair-value range at 234.35 to 279.84, which means today's price is at the top of it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the earlier 73.6B as the spending cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 24.65% a year in the latest quarter versus 21.79% two quarters ago, with trailing revenue of 471.1B.
The operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19%, so growth is not being bought with lower profitability.
Net cash of 139.0B gives plenty of room to keep investing through a weak cash-flow stretch.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, and the cash-flow model's base value is only 51.55 per share.
Analysts cut this year's EPS estimate by 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's 14.97 is below this year's 19.56, which lifts the forward P/E to 18.8.
The filings say the price needs about 36% a year growth against 17% a year delivered over 3 years, and price-to-sales of 7.4 is above the peer median of 4.7.

levels.what: Today's close, above 279.84. The stock is no longer cheap against its own past, so there is no new buying here. Keep the existing position.
Middle of the own-history range. Under the plan there is no adding above this price.
Low end of the own-history range and the add level. It leaves room for error if free cash flow stays near 19.7B.

longterm.why: Faster sales growth supports holding, but falling estimates and weak cash flow do not justify paying more than the middle of the stock's historical range. The plan stays: hold, and add only at 234.35.

swing.why: Today's close cleared the previous trigger of 277.07. Even so, the first ceiling at 293.72–300.07 is about as far away as a stop below 271.77, and that stop sits within one normal day's move (average true range, or ATR, of 11.92). Enter only if a pullback holds the 271.77–277.07 zone, or on a daily close above 300.07 with 304.97 as the next zone.

decision.timing: There is no earnings date in the data, so price levels and estimate changes set the timing. The December options imply a move of about 10.2% by 2026-12-18. The put/call open-interest ratio rose to 1.57, from 1.37 (more open bets on a fall than on a rise). The largest call positions sit at the 300 strike, which matches the 293.72–300.07 ceiling.

change_mind: A daily close back below 271.77 would mean today's rebound failed. The swing setup would be off, and the long-term plan would stay at adding only at 234.35.
If the next filing shows trailing free cash flow climbing from 19.7B back toward 73.6B, the cash-flow values would rise and the upper end of fair value could move toward 375.22.
If this year's EPS estimate stops falling (holding at 19.56 or rising, against the 5.2% cut over 30 days), the current price would be easier to justify. Further cuts would point back toward 234.35.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold. The 6.34% jump to 282.1 took the price above 279.84, the line where the plan says to stop adding, so it confirmed no new buying and left the add level at 234.35.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
